messages:
maria: Heads-up, perf regression on streaming p95 after the kernel selector change. Seeing spikes when users stream longer prompts (>1k tokens).

alex: repro steps? which kernel path is being chosen?

maria: looks like fallback to the generic GEMM kernel for sequences >1024 on A100 with the new selector heuristic. p95 jumped from 85ms -> 210ms on small requests when microbatching is enabled. p99 worse.

devon: that sounds like KV cache interaction — if the kernel switch also changes KV layout we might be invalidating cache lines and causing extra copies. Any traces?

maria: attached profiling snippet from a canary run (shortened):
```
# sample timeline (per-request)
0-10ms: recv + parse
10-40ms: kv lookup hit
40-120ms: kernel A (fast) for first chunk
120-250ms: kernel fallback + memcpy + barrier
250-300ms: emit tokens
```

sasha: interesting — the fallback adds ~100ms copy/handshake for mid-sequence chunks. That will wreck perceived latency for streaming where early tokens matter.

ken: what are our microbatch settings on those runs? batching can hide kernel overhead but hurts p95 for single active sessions.

maria: default microbatch_size=8, flush_interval_ms=25, chunk_tokens=16. We tried microbatch=32 and p99 throughput improved but p95 for single-session streaming got worse (users see token drip delayed).

alex: can we hack a two-tier flush: small immediate flush for first N tokens then aggregate? E.g. emit first 4 tokens with zero microbatching, then allow microbatching for the rest.

devon: yes, adaptive emit strategy. We prototyped a heuristic: if session prefix < 64 tokens or latency budget < 100ms, use per-request flush of chunk_size=4 and bypass microbatch. Otherwise use normal batching.

maria: ran the heuristic on canary. Results:
- baseline (mb=8, flush=25): p95=210ms, p99=480ms, throughput=86rps
- mb=32 (bulk): p95=320ms, p99=540ms, throughput=220rps
- adaptive (early-drip then batch): p95=95ms, p99=360ms, throughput=160rps

sasha: adaptive looks promising — reduces perceived latency for interactive sessions while preserving most throughput. Does it interact badly with KV cache hot paths?

maria: less copying overall because early tokens skip the kernel switch path by forcing the fast kernel (we add a kernel_hint for short-chunk emits). But we still see occasional tail spikes at p99 because when a large concurrent request arrives it forces a global kernel change on the node.

ken: that global kernel handoff is scary. Can we make kernel selection per-queue rather than global per-device? or have dual-kernel residency so both kernels can be placed in memory and we select without a heavy handshake?

devon: per-queue would reduce head-of-line impacts but increases memory pressure. Dual residency is feasible for smaller kernels, but for quantized kernels memory doubles. Need cost tradeoff.

alex: alternative: avoid full global handoff by routing long sequences to a separate pool of nodes that live with the fallback kernel already loaded. Short sequences stay on the fast-kernel pool. That keeps interactive p95 stable.

maria: routing idea seems low-risk operationally. It requires the smart router to look at expected sequence length or a cheap client hint. We can do quick client-side hint in the SDK for now ("expected_len").

ken: SDK hint + adaptive flush is good near-term. Medium-term: make kernel selector aware of latency SLO tags so it won't evict fast kernel off nodes that serve interactive tiers.

sasha: do we have telemetry to tie perceived latency complaints to chunk size/flush interval? We should add a token-level perceptual metric: time_to_first_token and drip_interval_variance per session.

maria: added metric in canary: time_to_first_token reduced from 180ms -> 80ms with adaptive. drip_interval_variance dropped by 60%.

ops-bot: deploy started: canary/adaptive-flush v0.3 -> runtime-canary-us-east-2 (rollout 10%).

devon: follow-ups:
- quick: add SDK expected_len hint + server-side router fallback (owner: alex)
- medium: implement node pools for long-seq routing + tests (owner: ken)
- infra: experiment with per-queue kernel residency to avoid global handoffs (owner: sasha)
- metrics: add time_to_first_token and drip_interval_variance, wire to alerts when p95 increases >2x (owner: maria)

alex: I'll open a PR for the SDK hint and router change. linking notes in the bug: <https://internal.redwood/iterations/RT-4123>

maria: thanks — main goal: keep p95 for interactive streaming <120ms while maintaining throughput. We'll monitor canary and measure p99 tails. :thumbsup:

ken: one more datapoint — kernel selector change was originally meant to reduce overhead for long-document beam decode. We should keep that benefit in the long-run; routing + adaptive flush seems the right compromise for now.

sasha: Agreed. Also let's add a small experiment to vary flush_interval_ms from 10->40 in A/B and measure perceived latency via time_to_first_token, not just p95.

maria: added to the follow-ups. Closing the thread when canary reaches stable metrics or we see new regressions.

alex: ping me if you need a quick patch for router probing logic.

maria: will do, thanks everyone.
